clue.text: Share expenses in journey from part of Europe

parts.note: a go can be a turn or trip, and to go is to journey
Dutch means from the Netherlands

explanation.surface: Travellers on a European trip agree to split the bills.
explanation.definitionFit: To go Dutch is the idiom for each person paying their own share of a meal or outing.

clue.text: Fail to get contract for warehouse

definitions.meaning: first meaning, as two words: in bridge, a declarer who falls short of the tricks bid
second meaning: an Anglo-Indian word for a storage building

explanation.surface: A company loses the bid to supply a storage depot.
explanation.walkthrough: The contract is a bridge contract; a declarer who makes too few tricks is said to go down.
explanation.definitionFit: In India and East Asia a godown is a warehouse, and the split phrase is bridge slang for failing.

clue.text: American port that's almost superfluous, it appears

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: de trop is French, used in English, for unwanted or excessive
taken as written

explanation.surface: An American harbour town seems nearly redundant.
explanation.definitionFit: Detroit is a Michigan city on the Detroit River, a working port on the Great Lakes waterway.

clue.text: Principles of marginal importance in court decisions

definitions.meaning: first meaning: fixed guidelines or rigid ways of thinking

definitions.text: of marginal importance in court decisions
definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the lines themselves
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the parallel lines at the edges of a tennis court, which matter for line calls

explanation.surface: Legal principles that matter little in judges' rulings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court decisions' suggests a law court; it is a tennis court, where the doubles side lines lie at the margin.
explanation.definitionFit: The word figuratively means fixed principles that govern behaviour, and literally names the paired side lines bordering a tennis court.

clue.text: Manuscript Darwin changed is in tenth revision

indicators.note: is in places one rearranged group inside the other
changed means altered, so the scientist's name is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a revision reworks something, so the other word is rearranged as well

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Darwin manuscript has been altered in its tenth edition.
explanation.definitionFit: Manuscript as an adjective means written by hand rather than typed or printed.

clue.text: Confirms what angry people have got

definitions.meaning: first meaning: supports or corroborates a claim
second meaning: an annoyed person is said to have their hackles raised, read literally as body parts raised

explanation.surface: Someone verifies what furious people are holding.
explanation.walkthrough: To have your back up is an idiom for being annoyed; the clue reads it literally as something angry people possess.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means supports or corroborates, as evidence does for a statement, and also names the raised backs of irritated people.

clue.text: Order a diamond, for example

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to command
second meaning: a call in bridge naming a trump suit, such as one diamond

explanation.surface: Someone requests a diamond, perhaps for an engagement ring.
explanation.walkthrough: The diamond is a bridge suit, not a jewel.
explanation.definitionFit: To bid is an old word for command, and in bridge an offer like one diamond is a bid.

clue.text: Shorten bird's tail? Rubbish!

indicators.note: shorten means cut down, here by removing the tail end of the word

parts.note: a common European finch
the last four letters of the bird, themselves a unit of length

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea of trimming a bird's tail feathers.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird's tail is INCH, so to shorten it by an inch is a neat joke on the deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaff is the husks separated from grain, so it figuratively means worthless material or nonsense.

clue.text: Girl brings in book with calculation to absorb in class

indicators.note: brings in means takes inside, so the girl's name holds the other pieces

parts.note: a girl's name
B is an abbreviation for book
a sum is a piece of arithmetic

explanation.surface: A schoolgirl brings a maths book to take in during lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Class' suggests a schoolroom; it means a category.
explanation.definitionFit: To subsume is to include something within a larger category or group.

clue.text: He takes off from Port Said as ordered

indicators.note: as ordered means put into a fresh sequence, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man sets off from the Egyptian port, as instructed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes off' looks like departing; it means imitating for comic effect.
explanation.definitionFit: A parodist mimics others' style mockingly, and to take someone off is an idiom for impersonating them.

clue.text: Stepped out of transport and arrested ringleader inside

indicators.note: inside says one piece sits within the other piece

parts.note: arrested means held by police
read as ring's leader: the letter at the front of ring

explanation.surface: A passenger got off a vehicle and then the police caught the gang's boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ringleader' looks like the gang boss but splits into the word ring and its leader, a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To detrain is to get off a railway train, so the past tense fits leaving that kind of transport.

clue.text: Warning light beam redirected to right

indicators.note: something redirected is sent another way, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
R is the usual abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A lamp's beam is turned to shine rightward as a signal.
explanation.definitionFit: On traffic signals the amber lamp warns drivers that the red stop signal is coming.

clue.text: How different sides feature in print

indicators.note: different means changed, so the letters of that word appear in a changed arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
the two sides are right and left, R and L

explanation.surface: A question about how opposing sides appear in newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: The print is a fingerprint, not printed text.
explanation.definitionFit: A whorl is a spiral ridge pattern, one of the standard patterns seen on fingerprints.

clue.text: Search for oil successful, being superbly equipped

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read as two words: a drilling hole located
second meaning: properly fitted out and supplied

explanation.surface: An oil exploration succeeds because the team had excellent gear.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyphenated adjective describes a ship or house fully provided with fittings, while the split phrase describes striking oil.

clue.text: People rowing may finish up at these turtles

definitions.text: People rowing may finish up at these
definitions.meaning: first meaning: quarrelling people end up at odds, in the idiom with at
second meaning: a large-headed sea turtle species

explanation.surface: Oarsmen might end up among turtles.
explanation.walkthrough: Rowing here means arguing, and to be at loggerheads is to be in dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: The loggerhead is a large sea turtle, and the idiom at loggerheads means in strong disagreement.

clue.text: Procedural rules for the suspension of sittings?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the permanent rules governing how a parliament or council conducts business

definitions.note: read cryptically as commands to get up
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: instructions telling seated people to rise

explanation.surface: A parliament's rulebook covering how sessions are adjourned.
explanation.walkthrough: Sittings sound like parliamentary sessions; the joke reads them as people sitting, and orders to stand stop that.
explanation.definitionFit: Assemblies call their permanent written procedures by this name, and literally the phrase means commands to get to your feet.

clue.text: Ordering a change in part of US border

indicators.note: a change rearranges something, so the letters are shuffled into new places

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone orders an alteration to a stretch of the American frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordering' looks like the anagram signal but is the fodder; 'change' does that job.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rio Grande river forms the frontier between Texas and Mexico for much of its length.

clue.text: A shift among its constituents could be alarming

definitions.text: A shift among its constituents could be alarming

indicators.note: a shift among a word's constituents moves its letters about, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written: the letters to be shifted

explanation.surface: A political observer warns that a small swing among voters in a seat could be worrying.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes a seat held by a small majority, where a small swing of voters loses it; the same words also rearrange the letters of alarming.
explanation.definitionFit: In British elections a seat won narrowly is called this, since a slight swing loses it.

clue.text: How men may be moved, in general

definitions.meaning: first meaning: chess or draughts pieces travel over the playing surface
second meaning: applying to everyone or everything equally

explanation.surface: A question about how soldiers are deployed by a commander in general.
explanation.walkthrough: Men are the pieces in chess or draughts, and 'general' tempts a military reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something applying universally, such as a pay rise for all staff, and literally the path of game pieces.

clue.text: Pickled fish, namely char, with bread

parts.note: a roll is a small loaf of bread
a char is a cleaning woman, known as Mrs Mop

explanation.surface: A menu offering pickled fish, specifically char, served with bread.
explanation.walkthrough: Char looks like the fish, but in Britain a char or charwoman is a cleaner, nicknamed Mrs Mop.
explanation.definitionFit: A rollmop is a herring fillet rolled around onion and preserved in spiced vinegar.

clue.text: Soldier in the pink

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a British soldier of the era of scarlet uniforms
second meaning: hunting pink is the scarlet jacket worn in foxhunting

explanation.surface: A soldier in excellent health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the pink' is an idiom for healthy, but pink here is the scarlet coat foxhunters wear.
explanation.definitionFit: British infantry once wore scarlet tunics, earning the nickname, and a hunting pink is literally a scarlet coat.

clue.text: This language may be said to be somebody's responsibility

indicators.note: may be said means spoken, so the word needed sounds like the one indicated

parts.note: the idiom that's not my pigeon means not my concern

explanation.surface: Someone claims a language is a particular person's job to handle.
explanation.walkthrough: In British idiom 'that's your pigeon' means that is your business or responsibility.
explanation.definitionFit: A pidgin is a simplified contact language that grows up between groups with no common tongue.

clue.text: Au fait, initially, with small island bird

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: initially points to the start of the neighbouring word, keeping only its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of fait
an inch is a Scottish word for a small island

explanation.surface: Someone familiar with a little island's bird life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Au fait' looks like a French phrase meaning well informed; split, Au is a chemical symbol and fait gives one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The goldfinch is a small European songbird with a red face and yellow wing bars.

clue.text: Make steady progress in fashion

definitions.meaning: first meaning: move forward gradually
second meaning: to shape metal by heating and hammering

explanation.surface: Someone advances steadily in the clothing industry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion' looks like the clothing world, but here it is the verb to shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A smith forges metal into shape, and a ship or runner forges forward steadily.

clue.text: Bones almost set without wires, I found

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a wireless set, the old name for a broadcast receiver
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone discovered that certain bones had nearly healed without surgical wiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set without wires' sounds like setting a fracture; it means a wireless set. RADII is the plural of RADIUS.
explanation.definitionFit: The radius is a forearm bone, and the Latin plural names more than one of them.

clue.text: Harlequin, for example, back in European city

indicators.note: back says read the letters from the end to the start

parts.note: Harlequins is a rugby union club, so one of its players is an RU man

explanation.surface: A pantomime clown makes a comeback in a continental town.
explanation.walkthrough: Harlequin looks like the pantomime character; it is a player for Harlequins, a London rugby union club, and RU is rugby union.
explanation.definitionFit: Namur is a city in Belgium, at the meeting of the Sambre and Meuse rivers.

clue.text: Performance by choir containing even number

parts.note: even and plain both mean flat, level or simple
a number is a piece of music in a performance

explanation.surface: A choral recital that includes an even-numbered item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' wants to be a figure; it is a musical piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Plainsong is unaccompanied liturgical chant sung in unison by a church choir.

clue.text: Whence you'll get pea, say, to serve up

definitions.text: Whence you'll get pea, say, to serve up

indicators.note: say means spoken, so the letter that sounds like the vegetable is taken

parts.note: the letter name sounds like the vegetable

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to do can mean to serve or suffice, as in that will do

explanation.surface: A cook explains where peas come from before dishing them up.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue says where a pea is got from to be served; the same words build the answer from a letter that sounds like pea and a reversed verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Peas grow inside a seed case that is split open to release them.

clue.text: Manage to see what someone is saying?

definitions.text: Manage to see what someone is saying

parts.words: Manage to see what someone is saying
parts.note: surface reading: understand someone's point of view
setter's reading: literally watch speech, following the movements of the mouth

explanation.walkthrough: 'I see what you're saying' is an idiom for understanding; the clue means seeing words physically on the speaker's mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Deaf people often follow conversation by watching mouth movements, interpreting words visually instead of hearing them.

clue.text: Swallowing small Scotch, an automatic way to remove bitterness

indicators.note: swallowing means taking something in, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the Sten is a British submachine gun
wee is Scots for small

explanation.surface: Taking a little whisky is a reflex way to soften a bitter mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small Scotch' suggests a dram of whisky, but it means the Scots word for small.
explanation.definitionFit: Adding sugar or honey makes a drink less sharp, so the verb fits taking away a bitter taste.
